title: Introduce per-model backpressure metrics and peek latency sparklines
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Added per-model backpressure and queue-depth metrics; new compact dashboard panels (peek latency sparklines); alert attenuation rules to reduce churn for transient bursts.
description: Summary: Add a lightweight per-model backpressure collector and a compact 'peek latency' sparkline for route dashboards to surface transient queueing without exploding cardinality. Motivation: operators are seeing noisy SLOs from short-lived queue spikes that correlate with heavy fanout prompts and prefetch bursts. Existing token-latency rollups miss microbursts and existing queue metrics are too coarse at model level. This change introduces: 1) a per-model queue-depth meter exposed as a histogram with device-level tags (model,region,instance_type); 2) a peek-latency sampler that collects sub-100ms percentiles for the head-of-line request path and exposes a compact sparkline JSON panel for dashboards; 3) alert attenuation and a 30s quiet-window policy that reduces pager churn for bursts under configured throughput thresholds. What changed (high level): - observability/collector/backpressure_collector.go: new collector with bounded in-memory reservoir to avoid cardinality explosion - observability/metrics/schema.yml: new metric definitions (model_queue_depth, peek_latency_ms_count, peek_latency_ms_sum) - observability/dashboards/peek-latency-sparklines.json: dashboard panel definition (compact, sparkline + lightweight tooltip linking to trace) - observability/alerting/attenuation_rules.yaml: staged attenuation rules and quiet-window configuration - telemetry/testing/synthetic_prefetch_replay.go: synthetic runner used to validate attenuation logic under bursty workloads Implementation notes: - The collector attaches to the request router's admission path and samples the head request of every 1 in N windows (configurable via env REDWOOD_PEEK_SAMPLE_RATE). Sampled items include minimal context (route, model, queue_depth, seq_len_bin) and are kept in a 2048-entry ring to bound memory. - Metrics use OTel histograms with explicit bucket set optimized for short-lived queue depths (0-64, powers of two) to avoid high-cardinality tagging. - The sparkline panel renders a compact 60-point series (1s resolution by default) and includes an action link that opens the sampled trace in the trace UI for deeper inspection. - The attenuation rules implement a two-stage suppressor: first a low-sensitivity suppression for bursts < 5x baseline and <30s, then an auto-escalate path if the burst sustains or correlates with increased error-rate. Testing performed: - Unit tests for collector boundary conditions and sample eviction (observability/collector/backpressure_collector_test.go) - End-to-end synthetic replay validation (telemetry/testing/replaybench) that exercises 10k requests/sec for 60s with prefetch patterns - Load bench in perf-canary with YAML config used to calibrate quiet-window thresholds Rollout plan: - Canary on staging and one small prod shard for 48h - Monitor: model_queue_depth p50/p99, peek_latency spike count, alert firing rate - Gradual rollout across regions with feature flag REDWOOD_OBS_BACKPRESSURE=on Related: Linear ENG-4621 (reduce alert churn from microbursts), ENG-4710 (dashboard compact units). Checklist: - [x] Collector implementation - [x] Dashboard panels - [x] Attenuation rules + tests - [x] Documentation snippets in docs/observability/backpressure.md - [x] Perf canary run and threshold calibration Manual verification steps: 1) Deploy with feature flag set on a single shard. 2) Run telemetry/testing/synthetic_prefetch_replay with short bursts and confirm peek_latency sparkline shows sub-second spikes. 3) Trigger a sustained load to verify attenuation step-up opens normal alert path. Links: - Dashboards: observability/dashboards/peek-latency-sparklines.json - Playbook: docs/ops/alert-attenuation-playbook.md
